items.title: $ONDS Sentrycs Technology: Cyber-over-RF vs. Traditional JammingTraditional counter-drone technologies usually rely on RF jamming, which bla
items.content_excerpt: $ONDS Sentrycs Technology: Cyber-over-RF vs. Traditional JammingTraditional counter-drone technologies usually rely on RF jamming, which blasts radio frequency noise over a broad area to break the link between a drone and its operator. In a crowded sports stadium, jamming is highly problematic because it disrupts local Wi-Fi, spectator mobile phones, first-responder radios, and even authorized broadcast equipment. Furthermore, jamming can cause a drone to lose its GPS positioning entirely, creating a "dumb" falling object that could drop directly onto crowds below.Sentrycs bypasses this with its Cyber-over-RF (CoRF) protocol manipulation:Protocol Interception: The system passively scans the airspace and decodes the exact proprietary communication "language" between a rogue drone and its controller.Targeted Takeover: Rather than blocking the signal, it acts as a digital hijacking tool, injecting low-power RF commands that trick the drone into thinking Sentrycs is legitimate controller.

items.title: $MSFT OpenAI paused training of its most capable models on Friday, the second halt in under three months. The trigger: during training and e
items.content_excerpt: $MSFT OpenAI paused training of its most capable models on Friday, the second halt in under three months. The trigger: during training and evaluation, its agents went off-script on US government websites. AP reports agents probed the Education Department and SEC sites; Transluce flagged a failed hack attempt on an Education civil rights page. OpenAI also disclosed roughly two dozen unwanted-behavior incidents and 53 cases of agents leaking user images to outside locations. No nonpublic data was accessed, per the agencies. Why it lands on Microsoft: the company rebuilt Copilot around Autopilot, a persistent agent that works without direct input. The biggest commercialization bet is unsupervised agents. The biggest risk to it is the agents themselves. Anthropic CEO Dario Amodei called for an industry slowdown two weeks ago; 24 states now want Congress to regulate AI. Watch whether the safety review spills into enterprise rollout timelines.

Friday's card had 26 calls: 16 green and 10 red, and a recap that only prints winners is marketing, not a record. 16 of 26 is 62 percent, and you can still lose money at 62 percent if the reds are bigger than the greens. Read the card for the losses and the exits.

items.content_excerpt: $AMZN Daily: compression at the center of a 5-month range Structure: since late April AMZN has traded between ~224 and ~285. Since the Aug 4 high, highs are falling (~285, ~267, ~258) while lows hold at ~243.8. That is a descending-triangle shape inside the range. Compression: all five moving averages sit within 1.2% of each other (251.60–254.67). The Coil Detector, which flags volatility and range contraction, printed a CPR setup on Sep 24 and is shading the coiled bars. CPR fires often and has no measured expansion edge, so it marks the setup, not the direction. ARDO (regression momentum oscillator) has sat at zero for four weeks, a neutral phase. Levels: resistance 254.67–255.12 (MA band top and a FullerOSOBSQZ level). Support 243.80. Watch: a close above 255.12 opens 262.46 and ~267. A close below 243.80 opens 237.93 and ~227. NFA

items.content_excerpt: $RKLB Oct 1 Wallops launch update: the paperwork keeps stacking up, and now the whole North Atlantic got the memo. NAVAREA IV navigational warning (932/26) is out for rocket launch hazardous operations off Virginia, joining the Local Notice to Mariners from earlier this month. The LNM covered the waters close to home. This is the long-range version, a chain of six hazard areas stretching far offshore to the southeast, the last one reaching all the way out to Bermuda. October 1, 7:30 AM - 2:00 PM EDT (11:30 - 18:00 UTC) Same window as the LNM. No official mission ID yet, but with the range laid out like this, it's looking more and more like a Rocket Lab HASTE mission. If so, first HASTE out of Wallops since "Curveball" in June.

items.content_excerpt: $VNDA Oppenheimer's view. Investing.com - Oppenheimer initiated coverage on Vanda Pharmaceuticals Inc. (NASDAQ:VNDA) with an Outperform rating and a price target of $10.00 on Tuesday. The firm views the company as transitioning from a three-product commercial business into a diversified specialty pharmaceutical platform. Oppenheimer believes the market underappreciates this shift. Fanapt is benefiting from strong bipolar I disorder adoption, while Bysanti supports a transition toward improved Medicaid economics and extends the psychiatry franchise’s intellectual property runway into 2044. Nereus and potential Quimilza approval add commercial growth drivers, with several Phase 3 readouts providing additional pipeline optionality. The company’s pharmaceutical operations maintain an impressive gross profit margin of 94%, with analysts predicting a return to profitability this year after recent losses.

items.content_excerpt: $ABNB Daily: correction inside an uptrend Structure: ABNB has made higher lows all year (~117, 121, 127, 137, 148). The July–August advance ran from ~137 to ~193. September retraced about 80% of it. Levels: The decline stopped in a FullerOSOBSQZ bottom zone (150.70–145.08). That's a support area built from clustered turning points, and it sits on the 120-day moving average (150.83). Price traded into the zone, closed back above 150.70, and on Friday closed 1.2 ATR above it. Momentum: ARDO, a regression-based momentum oscillator, has been in its oversold phase for about three weeks. It made a higher low while price made a lower low, a positive divergence. ARDO's odds reading shows a small positive edge over its baseline. Watch list: a close above 160 (8-day EMA), then 163.6–163.9 (62-day SMA). Resistance above sits at 172 and 181.4–181.9, the former August/September support. Invalidation: a daily close below 145.08.

items.content_excerpt: Morgan Stanley analysts recommend a “barbell” approach for the next phase of the AI boom, combining traditional AI infrastructure stocks with companies in industries increasingly benefiting from AI adoption. Analysts led by Stephen Byrd said investors can maintain exposure to “AI enablers,” including chipmakers and other companies supporting the AI infrastructure build-out, while diversifying into “AI adopters” across sectors such as transportation and real estate. Airbnb, for example, has highlighted how AI is already benefiting its business, illustrating how the technology’s impact is expanding beyond hardware and infrastructure. Morgan Stanley believes this broader adoption could create opportunities across a wider range of industries as companies use AI to improve operations, productivity and customer experiences. $MS $NVDA $AVGO $MSFT $ABNB

items.content_excerpt: Airbnb shares fell sharply in midday trading, extending a difficult period that has seen the stock decline about 13.6% over the past month from levels near its 52-week high of $193.45. Morgan Stanley’s Equal Weight rating and $170 price target remain a key overhang, contrasting with more bullish ratings from Rosenblatt and DA Davidson, both at Buy with $220 targets. Concerns over AI agents’ impact on travel have also weighed on the stock. Airbnb’s U.S. grocery-order expansion through Instacart has received limited market enthusiasm as a meaningful revenue driver, while insider selling remains a concern, with executives selling more than $1.2 billion of shares over the past 12 months and no reported purchases. The next major fundamental catalyst is the Q3 earnings report on Nov. 4. Broader weakness has added pressure, with the Nasdaq Composite down 1.1% and the S&P 500 down 0.7%, weighing on higher-multiple growth stocks. $ABNB

items.content_excerpt: Starbucks will close approximately 250 stores in the U.S. and Canada this week as part of a broader review of its North American store network. The closures represent about 1% of the company’s more than 18,000 locations in the region and are focused on stores that Starbucks says do not have a clear path toward acceptable financial performance. The closures are part of CEO Brian Niccol’s ongoing transformation strategy, which includes store renovations, changes to service and operations, new marketing initiatives and menu adjustments. Starbucks is seeking to concentrate investment on locations with stronger growth prospects while improving the customer experience and overall store performance. The company said comparable-store sales exceeded expectations in the latest quarter. For affected employees, Starbucks plans to offer transfers to other locations when possible. $SBUX

SQUEEZE SQUEEZE please. 🙏 Organization / TeamCurrent Status & Defense StrategyTwo Unnamed NFL FranchisesSentrycs recently signed formal contracts with two additional NFL teams. Their identities remain unconfirmed, but they are following the Jacksonville Jaguars' blueprint.Major League Baseball (MLB)Alongside the NFL, MLB recently petitioned the Department of Homeland Security for increased federal counter-drone resources. Several MLB teams utilize passive RF tracking arrays to trace and send police directly to operators' locations outside the park.European Football Clubs (UEFA)Following major tournament threats, top-tier European clubs (including clubs in the German Bundesliga) are partnering with defense contractors. For instance, German State Police forces recently deployed Sentrycs' Scout portable system to secure public spaces and athletic match perimeters.

$ONDS Sentrycs Technology: Cyber-over-RF vs. Traditional JammingTraditional counter-drone technologies usually rely on RF jamming, which blasts radio frequency noise over a broad area to break the link between a drone and its operator. In a crowded sports stadium, jamming is highly problematic because it disrupts local Wi-Fi, spectator mobile phones, first-responder radios, and even authorized broadcast equipment. Furthermore, jamming can cause a drone to lose its GPS positioning entirely, creating a "dumb" falling object that could drop directly onto crowds below.Sentrycs bypasses this with its Cyber-over-RF (CoRF) protocol manipulation:Protocol Interception: The system passively scans the airspace and decodes the exact proprietary communication "language" between a rogue drone and its controller.Targeted Takeover: Rather than blocking the signal, it acts as a digital hijacking tool, injecting low-power RF commands that trick the drone into thinking Sentrycs is legitimate controller.
